newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 1.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 1.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Newspapers reported on Thursday that the joint CBA-Schiphol bid for Brisbane airport was likely to be accepted while the Macquarie Bank-Serco-Manchester bid for Melbourne had missed out. AMP's bid with BAA Plc was likely to win the Melbourne bid, the newspapers said.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd said its sales revenue jumped to A$225.4 million in the first quarter of 1997 from A$156.8 million a year earlier. Woodside's figures in its quarterly report to the Australian Stock Exchange showed the rise in sales revenue largely reflected a jump in liquids sales to A$99.7 million in the first quarter from A$44.3 million a year earlier.
* Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd A$1.70 (+0.11)

Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd on Wednesday said it had made a major gold discovery at its Woodcutters tenements, about 40 km north of Kalgoorlie in Western Australia. The company also lifted the resource estimate at its Mt Pleasant and Ora Banda desposits in Western Australia by 1.8 million ounces to 5.7 million ounces.
* Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd SYD.AX. A$2.16 (-0.02)

Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd managing director Neil Gamble said Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) PBL.AX still intended to go ahead with its planned purchase of management control at the casino. "They have told us they are still going ahead," Sydney Casino chief executive officer Neil Gamble told Reuters.
* F.H. Faulding & Co Ltd FHX.AX A$7.92 (+0.14)

Fauldings's U.S. unit reported third quarter earnings results overnight. Q3 gross profit rose to US$8.8 million from US$4.3 million in the same quarter a year earlier while net earnings per share rose to five cents per share from a loss of 18 cents a share a year earlier.

JCI Ltd announced on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement with Star Mining Corp NL to develop the Russian Sukhoi Log gold deposit. The transaction will entail JCI subscribing for $7.5 million worth of Star shares, providing a guarantee allowing the advance of a $50 million loan to a Star unit and subscribing for shares and loan notes in that unit for an amount of $170 million. JCI's subscription for $7.5 million of Star shares will take place in three tranches. The first would be $3.0 million immediately at an issue price of 18 Australian cents per share.
Pasminco Ltd said on Wednesday that mining at its Elura lead-zinc mine in New South Wales was suspended as a precautionary measure on Wednesday following pillar damage caused by blasting.
